about: ic's channel records (the text it writes under its home) and, for each, the swap row `ic sandbox swaps --json` answers at `now`: null when the record names no swap. `ic` owns the rule (probation.rs cutover_in_progress: a cutover is in progress while its own heartbeat, else its start, is under staleMs old); the device agent's fallback for an ic without the command is held to the same rows. Tested in Rust (ic/src/sandbox/swaps.rs) and TS (devices/machine swap-records.test.ts, the contract's device-swaps.test.ts).

cases.name: a cutover that began a moment ago, with no heartbeat yet, is in progress
one millisecond short of the stale age it is still in progress
at exactly the stale age it is interrupted
a cutover with no heartbeat, left for half an hour (an ic killed mid-swap), is interrupted
a fresh heartbeat keeps a long cutover in progress
a heartbeat that stopped makes a recent cutover interrupted: the heartbeat, not the start, is what counts
one millisecond short of a stale heartbeat it is still in progress
a stamp from the future (a clock that moved back) reads as just now
a heartbeat of nought is a heartbeat from 1970, not an absent one
a heartbeat that is not a number is no heartbeat: the start is judged
a probation is never a cutover in progress, however recent, and names when it ends
the last occurrence of a key wins, and a CRLF record reads like an LF one
a phase with no start time is no swap
a start time that is not a number is no swap
a phase this ic does not know is no swap
a record with no swap keys is no swap
